stem: When a child completes an online exercise called a Mathlit, they might be awarded a medal. The publishers claim that the probability that a randomly chosen child who completes a Mathlit will be awarded a medal is $\frac{1}{3}$. Asha wishes to test this claim. She decides that if she is awarded no medals while completing 10 Mathlits, she will conclude that the true probability is less than $\frac{1}{3}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Use a binomial distribution to find the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The true probability of being awarded a medal is denoted by $p$.
parts.text: Given that the probability of a Type II error is 0.8926, find the value of $p$.
